concepts.title: School buses: ordinary two-lane roads
concepts.summary: On an ordinary two-lane, two-way road, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus receiving or discharging passengers with its red lights flashing.

concepts.title: School buses: two travel lanes plus a turn lane
concepts.summary: One travel lane in each direction plus a center turn lane is the handbook’s two-lane-with-center-turn-lane configuration. Both directions must stop.

concepts.title: School buses: four undivided travel lanes
concepts.summary: On a four-lane road without a median separation or center turning lane, traffic from both directions must stop for a school bus loading or unloading with red lights flashing.

concepts.title: School buses: four travel lanes plus a turn lane
concepts.summary: With four or more ordinary travel lanes plus a center turning lane, only traffic following the stopped school bus must stop under the school-bus rule. Opposing drivers must still watch for people and other hazards.

concepts.title: School buses: median-separated highways
concepts.summary: On a divided highway with four or more lanes and a median separation, only traffic following the school bus must stop under this rule.

concepts.title: Following a stopped school bus
concepts.summary: The divided-road and qualifying center-turn-lane exceptions concern opposing traffic. Drivers traveling behind a school bus must stop when it stops for passengers with red lights flashing.

concepts.title: School-bus red lights and stop arm
concepts.summary: A bus’s flashing red lights or mechanical stop signal while it receives or discharges passengers requires approaching traffic subject to the rule to stop; both signals need not appear together.

concepts.title: When to resume after a school-bus stop
concepts.summary: The handbook instructs stopped drivers not to pass until the bus’s stop signal is withdrawn, its flashing red lights are off, and the bus has started moving.

concepts.title: School-bus maximum speed
concepts.summary: The handbook gives ordinary school buses a maximum of 45 mph. A lower posted limit still controls. School activity buses have a separate 55 mph maximum.

concepts.title: School activity-bus maximum speed
concepts.summary: The handbook gives a school activity bus a maximum of 55 mph; a lower posted limit still applies. This differs from the ordinary school-bus maximum of 45 mph.

concepts.title: School buses at railroad crossings
concepts.summary: The handbook identifies school buses as vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings. Drivers following a bus should anticipate that stop.

concepts.title: Children near school-bus stops
concepts.summary: Children around a school-bus stop may run into the roadway unexpectedly even when the bus is not visible. Driver vigilance is not limited to flashing-light situations.

concepts.title: Where to stop at a STOP sign
concepts.summary: Without a stop line or marked crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection at a location with a view of the intersecting street.

concepts.title: Flashing red signals
concepts.summary: A flashing red traffic signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield as required, then proceed when safe.

concepts.title: Flashing yellow signals
concepts.summary: A flashing circular yellow signal tells drivers to reduce speed and continue with caution; it does not require an automatic stop like flashing red.

concepts.title: Steady yellow signals
concepts.summary: A steady yellow warns that red is coming. Stop when you can safely do so; never accelerate to beat the light.

concepts.title: Right turns on red
concepts.summary: At a steady circular red, a right turn is normally permitted after a complete stop and yielding to vehicles and pedestrians unless a sign prohibits it.

concepts.title: Left turns on a circular green
concepts.summary: A left turn on a circular green is not a protected green-arrow movement. Yield to conflicting oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

concepts.title: Flashing yellow turn arrows
concepts.summary: A flashing yellow arrow permits the indicated turn after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. It is not a protected movement.

concepts.title: Red arrows alongside circular green signals
concepts.summary: When a circular signal and a turn arrow appear together, the arrow governs its turning movement. A solid red left-turn arrow prohibits that left turn.

concepts.title: Steady yellow turn arrows
concepts.summary: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected green-arrow phase is ending. Prepare to stop rather than accelerating to complete a new turn.

concepts.title: A traffic signal that has gone dark
concepts.summary: A malfunctioning intersection signal with no officer or other control is treated as an all-way stop. A dark ramp meter has a different specific rule.

concepts.title: An officer directing traffic
concepts.summary: An officer directing traffic takes precedence over the normal signals or signs at that location.

concepts.title: A dark ramp meter
concepts.summary: A dark ramp meter displaying neither red nor green allows normal ramp use: merge or yield as conditions require, without a stop solely for the dark meter.

concepts.title: A red ramp meter
concepts.summary: A steady red ramp-meter indication requires a stop and a wait for green before continuing down the ramp.

concepts.title: Pedestrian beacon: flashing-red phase
concepts.summary: During the alternating flashing-red phase of a pedestrian hybrid beacon, first stop completely; then proceed when the crossing is clear.

concepts.title: Simultaneous arrival at an uncontrolled intersection
concepts.summary: At an uncontrolled intersection, simultaneous arrivals yield to the vehicle on the right. This is different from a vehicle already occupying the intersection.

concepts.title: A vehicle already in the intersection
concepts.summary: A vehicle already in an uncontrolled intersection has priority over a vehicle that has not entered. The simultaneous-arrival rule does not displace it.

concepts.title: An intersection with obstructed views
concepts.summary: At an unmarked intersection with poor visibility in all directions, the handbook advises stopping before moving forward slowly and cautiously.

concepts.title: Leaving a private driveway
concepts.summary: When leaving a private driveway, stop and yield to vehicles and pedestrians before entering the public roadway.

concepts.title: Pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks
concepts.summary: At an intersection without traffic signals, pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks have right of way. Unmarked crosswalks can follow the imaginary continuation of sidewalks.

concepts.title: Pedestrians completing a crossing
concepts.summary: A pedestrian who entered lawfully must be allowed to finish crossing safely even if the signal changes during the crossing.

concepts.title: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog
concepts.summary: The handbook gives special consideration at unsignalized intersections to blind pedestrians using a white cane, a white cane with a red tip, or a guide dog.

concepts.title: Yielding to a funeral procession
concepts.summary: Do not enter across the path of a funeral procession continuing through an intersection after its lead vehicle entered lawfully, even if you face green. Safe entry that does not cross its path is treated differently.

concepts.title: Conflicting U-turn and right-turn arrows
concepts.summary: Where a U-turn and an opposing right turn are both allowed by simultaneous green arrows, U-turning traffic should yield to the opposing right-turning traffic.

concepts.title: Entering a roundabout
concepts.summary: When entering a roundabout, yield to vehicles and bicyclists already circulating. Do not pass a bicyclist within the roundabout.

concepts.title: Pedestrians at a roundabout exit
concepts.summary: When leaving a roundabout, signal your exit and yield to pedestrians in the exit crosswalk. Priority over entering vehicles does not override crosswalk duties.

concepts.title: Keeping right on an interstate
concepts.summary: The handbook advises keeping right on the interstate and using the left lane or lanes for passing.

concepts.title: Lane changes inside intersections
concepts.summary: The handbook says not to change lanes while moving straight through an intersection. Complete the crossing before making a safe lane change.

concepts.title: Checking the lane beyond your target
concepts.summary: On a multilane road, check the lane beyond the one you want to enter: another driver may be moving from that lane toward the same space.

concepts.title: Through lanes on one-way streets
concepts.summary: For a multilane one-way street, the handbook recommends center lanes for through travel and outside lanes for turning.

concepts.title: Being in the wrong lane for a turn
concepts.summary: When you cannot safely get into the proper turning lane, continue to a later intersection rather than making an improper or forced turn.

concepts.title: Two-way center left-turn lanes
concepts.summary: A two-way center left-turn lane is reserved for left-turn movements. The handbook says not to use it for passing or for merging into through traffic.

concepts.title: Passing lanes on three-lane highways
concepts.summary: On a three-lane highway of the type described by the handbook, use the center lane to pass only where it is marked for passing in your direction. A shared left-turn lane is different.

concepts.title: Yellow and white pavement lines
concepts.summary: Yellow markings generally separate opposing traffic. White lane markings generally separate traffic moving in the same direction.

concepts.title: Passing across a broken yellow line
concepts.summary: A broken yellow centerline on your side allows passing only when the way is clear and other location-specific restrictions do not prohibit it.

concepts.title: A solid yellow line on your side
concepts.summary: When a solid yellow line is on your side and a broken yellow line is on the opposite side, the broken-line permission applies to the other direction, not yours.

concepts.title: A vehicle stopped for a pedestrian
concepts.summary: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. A pedestrian can be hidden from the passing driver’s view.

concepts.title: Returning to your lane after passing
concepts.summary: A pass is not safe if the driver you passed must slow down to let you return to the correct lane. Leave adequate room before moving back.

concepts.title: Helping another vehicle pass
concepts.summary: Help a passing driver complete the maneuver safely; move toward the right edge as appropriate and do not increase speed while being passed.

concepts.title: Passing on the right on one-way streets
concepts.summary: The handbook lists one-way streets with all lanes moving in the same direction among situations where a safe pass on the right is allowed.

concepts.title: Passing a vehicle in a left-turn lane
concepts.summary: A vehicle in a left-turn lane may be passed on the right using a lawful lane when conditions are safe. This does not create permission to use an unsafe shoulder route.

concepts.title: Passing on the right on multilane highways
concepts.summary: The handbook includes highways with at least two lanes in each direction among layouts where safe passing on the right is allowed in lawful travel lanes.

concepts.title: Advance turn signals at higher speed
concepts.summary: The handbook calls for signaling at least the final 200 feet before a turn when the road’s speed limit is 45 mph or higher; its general minimum is 100 feet.

concepts.title: Entering using an acceleration lane
concepts.summary: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of interstate traffic and merge safely. Reaching an appropriate speed does not remove the need to yield and choose a gap.

concepts.title: Exiting using a deceleration lane
concepts.summary: Signal in advance, move into the deceleration lane without slowing on the freeway, then reduce speed for the posted exit speed.

concepts.title: Missing an interstate exit
concepts.summary: After missing an interstate exit, continue to the next exit and use a suitable route to return. Do not back up or make an improvised turn across the median.

concepts.title: An approaching emergency vehicle
concepts.summary: For an approaching emergency vehicle using lights and siren on an ordinary roadway, move to the right edge and stop safely until it passes or an officer directs otherwise.

concepts.title: Emergency vehicles across a divided highway
concepts.summary: The handbook exempts opposing traffic on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median from the usual opposite-direction emergency-vehicle yielding requirement.

concepts.title: Move Over: another lane is available
concepts.summary: When safely possible on a highway with at least two lanes in your direction, move away from the lane nearest a qualifying stopped emergency or service vehicle displaying warning lights.

concepts.title: Move Over: only one same-direction lane
concepts.summary: With only one lane traveling in your direction, slow to a reduced, safe speed until completely past a qualifying stopped emergency or public service vehicle with warning lights.

concepts.title: Emergency vehicles while in a roundabout
concepts.summary: When already inside a roundabout and an emergency vehicle approaches, exit the roundabout first, then pull over to let it pass.

concepts.title: Fire hoses across the roadway
concepts.summary: The handbook instructs motorists not to drive over a fire hose. Do not treat it as an obstacle to cross slowly.

concepts.title: Parking near a stopped emergency vehicle
concepts.summary: The handbook says not to park within 100 feet of an emergency vehicle stopped to investigate a crash or provide assistance.

concepts.title: Space around a responding fire truck
concepts.summary: The handbook says not to drive or park closer than one block from a fire truck responding to a fire alarm. This differs from parking near an already stopped emergency vehicle.

concepts.title: Controlling a tire blowout
concepts.summary: After a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, maintain a straight path, and ease off the accelerator. Delay braking until speed is low enough to remain controlled, then leave the road safely.

concepts.title: Wheels leaving the pavement
concepts.summary: If wheels leave the pavement, avoid an immediate hard brake or sharp return. Ease off the accelerator, steer straight, slow substantially, and return gradually when safe.

concepts.title: A stuck accelerator
concepts.summary: For a stuck accelerator, try to release the pedal, shift to neutral, brake firmly without locking the wheels, and move safely off the roadway.

concepts.title: Brake failure: automatic transmission
concepts.summary: For service-brake failure in an automatic-transmission vehicle, the handbook directs use of the emergency brake and a low transmission range.

concepts.title: Brake failure: manual transmission
concepts.summary: For service-brake failure in a manual-transmission vehicle, the handbook says to shift to a lower gear, release the clutch to use engine braking, and apply the emergency brake.

concepts.title: Emergency braking with ABS
concepts.summary: For an emergency stop with ABS, brake hard and keep firm, steady pressure. Pumping the pedal reduces the system’s effectiveness.

concepts.title: Slippery-road braking without ABS
concepts.summary: For slippery-road braking without ABS, the handbook describes gently pumping the brakes to reduce the risk of locking the wheels. This differs from its steady-pressure ABS technique.

concepts.title: An oncoming vehicle in your lane
concepts.summary: If an oncoming vehicle enters your path, reduce speed, sound the horn, and keep right, even if leaving the roadway becomes necessary.

concepts.title: Finding a safe place for a traffic stop
concepts.summary: When an officer signals a stop but no safe stopping place is immediately available, the handbook recommends four-way flashers, reducing speed by about 10 mph, and continuing lawfully to the nearest safe stopping place.

concepts.title: Leaving a vehicle stalled on tracks
concepts.summary: If a vehicle stalls on or near railroad tracks, get everyone out immediately and move well away from the vehicle and tracks. Report the emergency after reaching safety.

concepts.title: Reporting a railroad emergency
concepts.summary: After reaching safety from a railroad crossing emergency, use the blue Emergency Notification System sign’s contact and crossing information to notify the railroad.

concepts.title: A train’s right of way
concepts.summary: Trains have right of way over highway traffic, including police, fire, and ambulance vehicles responding to emergencies.

concepts.title: Passengers during a tire change
concepts.summary: For a roadside tire change, the handbook advises passengers to leave on the passenger side and move away from the road or shoulder and from the front and rear of the vehicle.

concepts.title: Headlights when using wipers in rain
concepts.summary: Use headlights when windshield wipers are operating because of inclement weather, including daytime rain.

concepts.title: Slippery pavement when rain begins
concepts.summary: The beginning of rain can be especially slippery as water mixes with accumulated surface material. The handbook highlights the first 10–15 minutes and advises lower speed and more following room.

concepts.title: Recovering from hydroplaning
concepts.summary: If the vehicle hydroplanes, ease off the accelerator, avoid braking, and keep the steering wheel straight while slowing enough to regain tire contact.

concepts.title: Drying wet brakes
concepts.summary: After water reduces brake effectiveness, the handbook describes driving a short distance with light brake pressure to create friction and help dry the brake linings.

concepts.title: Steering when the rear starts to skid
concepts.summary: For a rear-wheel skid, initially steer in the direction the rear is sliding, then correct as the vehicle straightens. Avoid abrupt overcorrection.

concepts.title: The two-second following rule
concepts.summary: The handbook’s two-second rule measures time between the vehicle ahead passing a fixed point and your vehicle reaching it. Conditions can require a larger gap.

concepts.title: Following distance on wet roads
concepts.summary: In wet conditions, the handbook advises at least twice the normal following distance and an appropriate reduction in speed.

concepts.title: The default city and town speed limit
concepts.summary: The handbook lists 35 mph as the general speed limit in cities and towns unless otherwise posted. Conditions may require driving more slowly.

concepts.title: Stopping distance at 55 mph
concepts.summary: The handbook gives approximately 211 feet to stop from 55 mph even under ideal conditions. This is an estimate, not a guarantee for every vehicle and surface.

concepts.title: Passing a motorcycle
concepts.summary: A motorcycle is entitled to its full lane. Change lanes to pass it as you would a larger motor vehicle, rather than squeezing past within the lane.

concepts.title: Passing a bicyclist
concepts.summary: The handbook advises passing a bicyclist only with abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic in the opposing lane; changing lanes is the safest method.

concepts.title: Wrong-way travel and edge-line colors
concepts.summary: On a divided highway, the right edge is normally white and the left edge yellow. Seeing the yellow edge on your right and white edge on your left indicates wrong-way travel.

concepts.title: Red pavement reflectors
concepts.summary: Red reflective pavement markers facing a driver indicate wrong-way movement. Blue markers can identify nearby firefighting water supplies.

concepts.title: STOP sign
concepts.summary: The red octagonal STOP sign is a regulatory instruction to stop.

concepts.title: YIELD sign
concepts.summary: The downward-pointing red-and-white triangle is the YIELD sign.

concepts.title: DO NOT ENTER sign
concepts.summary: The white rectangular sign with a red circle and horizontal white bar marks DO NOT ENTER.

concepts.title: NO LEFT TURN sign
concepts.summary: The red circle and slash over a left-turn arrow means NO LEFT TURN.

concepts.title: NO U-TURN sign
concepts.summary: The red circle and slash over a U-shaped arrow means NO U-TURN.

concepts.title: LEFT TURN ONLY sign
concepts.summary: A left arrow with ONLY is a lane-use instruction requiring the left turn from that lane.

concepts.title: Straight or left-turn lane sign
concepts.summary: The combined straight and left arrow permits either of those movements from the indicated lane.

concepts.title: KEEP RIGHT sign
concepts.summary: KEEP RIGHT directs traffic around the right side of an obstruction or divider.

concepts.title: ONE WAY sign
concepts.summary: The ONE WAY sign identifies the allowed direction of travel.

concepts.title: DO NOT PASS sign
concepts.summary: DO NOT PASS is a regulatory passing restriction.

concepts.title: KEEP OFF MEDIAN sign
concepts.summary: KEEP OFF MEDIAN directs drivers not to use the median.

concepts.title: DO NOT STOP ON TRACKS sign
concepts.summary: The handbook excerpt explicitly identifies this sign as a reminder not to stop on the railroad track for any reason.

concepts.title: Railroad crossing advance warning
concepts.summary: The yellow circle with an X and RR is the railroad-crossing advance warning.

concepts.title: NO PASSING ZONE pennant
concepts.summary: The yellow pennant is the NO PASSING ZONE warning.

concepts.title: STOP AHEAD warning
concepts.summary: A yellow diamond with an upward arrow and a red octagon warns of a STOP sign ahead.

concepts.title: Signal ahead warning
concepts.summary: The traffic-light symbol on a yellow diamond warns of a signal ahead.

concepts.title: Merging traffic warning
concepts.summary: The merging-traffic warning shows a stream of traffic joining the main roadway.

concepts.title: Lane ends warning
concepts.summary: The lane-drop warning alerts drivers that a travel lane ends.

concepts.title: Two-way traffic warning
concepts.summary: Opposing up-and-down arrows on a yellow diamond warn of two-way traffic.

concepts.title: SOFT SHOULDER warning
concepts.summary: SOFT SHOULDER warns about the shoulder’s condition, not a new lane for driving.

concepts.title: Low-clearance warning
concepts.summary: LOW CLEARANCE warns of a vertical limit ahead; compare the indicated height with the vehicle’s height.

concepts.title: Crossroad warning
concepts.summary: A black cross on a yellow diamond warns of a crossroad intersection.

choices.text: Stop for the bus.
choices.feedback: On an ordinary two-lane, two-way road, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus receiving or discharging passengers with its red lights flashing.
